judgements.justification: Both area chairs followed their reviewers' scores: A's two-sentence meta-review follows the 6.5 mean to a poster, and B's restates its reviewers' agreement; neither substituted its own reading.
No reviewer or area chair on either side forecast impact beyond the paper's own setting; B's 'timely, significant, and relevant' is a reviewer's assessment of the paper itself.
The rebuttal moved scores in both committees (A's Reviewer_7pq7 and Reviewer_4Rfw, B's Reviewer_d46C), so it did not move one committee and leave the other unchanged.
A's Reviewer_4Rfw spent 1.5 h on three one-line questions and Reviewer_5o85 gave one specific point and never replied, both rating 6; A totals about 13 reviewer-hours against B's 23.

The one-sided issues (A's GP baseline and VEM bias; B's Eq. (12), Pontryagin, mode mismatch) changed no score; the weaknesses that held A's 6s down (no baseline, qualitative results, scaling) were shared.

Both committees named the same faults (no baseline, qualitative 1D/2D results, Sec. 4.1 parameter bias, linear drift only); B's reviewers called them camera-ready work and rated 7-8, while A's 6s held them against the paper.
No reviewer in either committee changed a score after reading other reviewers; the score moves followed the authors' replies.
Each rating matches its text: A's 6s carry stated reservations, and B's naZJ and czKb list weaknesses but write 'accept' with 7; QSy5's 8 is thin, not out of line with its positive text.
A's Reviewer_7pq7 said they were 'not familiar with the literature' and rated 6, and A's three 6s all came at confidence 3, holding A's mean at 6.5 near the threshold.
Neither area chair followed a single outlier: A's meta-review ignores its outlier x8VX, and B has no outlier.

B's naZJ and czKb list almost exactly A's weaknesses yet rate 7 ('Good paper, accept') where A's similar assessments sit at 6, and each area chair followed its mean (6.5 vs 7.25) to poster and spotlight.
B's spotlight follows a higher mean (7.25 vs 6.5) and includes an 8; A's maximum is also 8, so B's agreement did not lift it over a committee with a similar or higher mean.
B's d46C raised on the authors' explanations of the formulation, not on unverified results; A's raises rested on the argument that no hybrid baseline exists, not on new evidence.

A's meta-review carries cost and related-work requests and B's lists the parameter-error study and Eq. (12) as revisions; neither stated the opposite of its reviewers' weaknesses in a way that drove the tier.
B's czKb (Eq. (12)) and naZJ (observations absent from figures) made wrong claims, but neither fed a score: czKb kept 7 and called it likely notation, and the figure point is minor.
No rebuttal conceded an unfavourable result; the authors argued that a hybrid baseline does not exist and explained costs.
czKb's post-rebuttal note of 2021-08-31 kept 'should be accepted' and lowered no score; no late objection stood unanswered against the paper.
The score profiles differ (6, 6, 6, 8 vs 8, 7, 7, 7; means 6.5 vs 7.25), so the split follows the reviews, not area chairs' thresholds on near-identical scores.

added.name: Area chair passed over the expert reviewer's verdict
added.definition: One committee's best-informed reviewer (highest confidence, most specific review) reached a verdict that the area chair neither cited nor weighed, following instead the mean of less-informed reviewers' scores, so the recommendation reflected the less-informed majority.
added.justification: R09 names the unsure reviewers' borderline scores and R10 names an area chair who follows an outlier; no reason names an area chair who averages over the committee's only expert, whose 8 and specific review go unmentioned while the thin 6s set the tier.

reasoning: Both committees saw the same paper and the same faults; the split comes from how each committee's reviewers placed them on the scale and from who reviewed. B's reviewers wrote A's weaknesses and still rated 7-8 (R06, R11). A's three 6s came from thin or unsure reviews (R04, R09), and A's area chair followed their mean while ignoring the committee's only expert, whose 8 was the best-argued score in A; no existing reason names that aggregation failure, so I added R19. The rebuttal moved scores on both sides, wrong claims in B fed no score, and the score profiles differ, so R03, R15 and R18 do not apply.
